root_idea.summary: The root centers on heaviness and sluggishness that make one refrain from an action or fail to complete it.
root_idea.development: This core develops into ordinary laziness and indolence, causative rendering of someone heavy or sluggish, and a specialized sexual usage denoting penetration without emission.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic plural is normalized to the supported singular adjective citation form كَسْلَانٌ.

senses.definition: Lazy, sluggish, or lacking active willingness in performing an action.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is the plural كُسَالَىٰ, used of people who come to or stand for prayer in a sluggish, unenergetic manner.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone heavy, sluggish, lazy, indolent, or torpid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II; the supplied lexical evidence specifically describes the effect of satiety.
A specialized Form IV construction, supplied with عَنْهَا in the expression أَكْسَلَ عَنْهَا.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Form II causative meaning is represented as a Classical Arabic meaning.
